title: The Conditions
description: MNHS describes three conditions: arriving criminals identified themselves, paid, and avoided major crimes inside Saint Paul. These are a historian’s summary of an informal arrangement, not reproduced clauses of a signed agreement.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: No universal compliance, crime-reduction measurement, or signed contract established.

title: The Intermediary
description: MNHS places Griffin before Hogan in the intermediary role and associates Hogan with the Green Lantern. This chronology connects people and places without putting Griffin in Hogan’s later saloon.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: Succession is not proof of a personal meeting between Griffin and Hogan.

title: The Money Trail
description: The 1935 appellate opinion upheld the convictions for 1929 and 1930 and notes the jury’s acquittal on the 1931 count. It distinguishes bank deposits from taxable income and examines competing financial explanations.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: The partial acquittal preceded the appeal; the court did not treat all deposits as income.

title: The Jury and the Loans
description: The 1938 opinion affirmed Gleckman’s criminal-contempt convictions. It describes a promised $300 payment to juror Bernard Fuchs through intermediaries and a later loan arranged at Gleckman’s direction. It does not establish a separate conviction of Fuchs.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: The findings concern Gleckman. Do not assign Fuchs an unverified legal outcome.

title: The 1933 Notice
description: Commercial West published a notice for Castle Royal, Inc. on September 30, 1933. The announcement names business purposes including restaurants, cafes, taverns, and nightclubs. This is a paraphrase of the notice, not an original charter or a facsimile.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: The business notice does not establish patrons or prove that this is the original incorporation filing.

title: A Guest List Without a Register
description: Brick discusses conflicting recollections around the venue’s 1977 revival and reports the lack of proof for named gangster attendance. Later recollections are evidence of disagreement; they are not a contemporary guest register.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: Disputed guest stories remain disputed; no origin date or intentional invention is established.

title: A Person and an Uncertain Footprint

sourceLocators.locator: Hamm abduction narrative; setting differs from S08

description: The RCHS account records Hamm’s kidnapping, $100,000 ransom, and release. It associates the abduction with a former family residence at 671 Cable Street. The FBI retrospective instead describes him leaving his office. The tour retains this unresolved difference.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: Released alive does not mean unharmed. The exact abduction location remains unresolved.

title: The Message Becomes Evidence
description: The FBI retrospective describes applying silver nitrate solution to ransom material to reveal fingerprints. This paraphrase describes the reported method without claiming priority over every earlier forensic investigation.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: Agency retrospective; neither a laboratory report examined here nor a claim of global forensic priority.

title: A Demand Is Not Compliance
description: The 1936 Bremer summary records threats intended to deter police contact and also reports immediate notification of local and federal authorities. A demand for secrecy is therefore different from evidence of compliance.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: Threats describe coercion; they are not trustworthy promises about the victim’s fate.

title: Changing the Target
description: The investigative summary attributes to Harry Sawyer a preference for kidnapping Bremer over robbing his bank because he expected a greater return. This is investigators’ reconstruction, not a recording of the planning conversation.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: An attributed investigative reconstruction cannot supply every participant’s private reasoning.

title: A Boundary Changes the Case

sourceLocators.locator: FBI Dillinger overview, Bureau Joins the Hunt

description: The FBI account links active federal pursuit of Dillinger to interstate transportation of a stolen car. It supplies a particular basis for that pursuit, not a claim that all earlier federal assistance was impossible.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: No apartment-specific protection agreement has been established.

title: Report, Surveillance, Confrontation
description: The FBI account places the manager’s report on March 30, 1934, and surveillance and confrontation the next day. It describes Dillinger’s wounded escape with Frechette. The tour does not supply an exact time, apartment plan, or independently verified line of fire.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: No checked floor plan, exact time of confrontation, or exhaustive witness comparison.

title: Name the Actual Outcome

sourceLocators.locator: Frechette paragraph in the retrospective case history

description: The FBI retrospective reports Frechette’s conviction and sentence for conspiracy to harbor a fugitive. Separately, the Gleckman appellate opinions establish tax and contempt outcomes. These sources support named outcomes, not a claim that everyone associated with the defendants was convicted.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: An agency history is different from an original judgment. Each legal outcome must retain its own attribution.

title: Change the Appointment Rule
description: MNHS describes a 1935 wiretap investigation and the June 15, 1936 charter amendment changing police-chief selection and tenure. Institutional rules and individual convictions address different parts of the problem.
supports: The bounded claim or attributed account linked below.
limits: Reform changed formal rules; it does not establish that all corruption disappeared.
